correctness.rationale: Checked the precise 16-letter block B(x,y)=1101100x1100100y, arbitrary x_j and y_1..y_{q-1}, fixed terminal y_q=1, q>=1. The greedy-subsequence endpoint transition is monotone in its start position. The bounded six-input local lemma exhausts 64 binary inputs in four initial and eight subsequent bit contexts, yielding exactly two paths to the extremal next-block endpoint and a strict >=2-position gap otherwise; a prior subextremal path cannot catch up. Induction doubles the extremal count to 2^q at length 6q. Since the prefix ends in 01, both binary extensions from any nonterminal endpoint can be embedded, whereas both extensions from each extremal endpoint fail: universality 6q, shortest-absent count 2^(q+1). Arithmetic odd-part paperfolding fixes 14 symbols of each 16-block and f(2^k)=1, so q=2^(k-4) and the dyadic formulas follow. Independently implemented greedy automaton and enumerated all 170 free-bit assignments over q=1..4, agreeing in all cases; the local finite lemma plus induction proves the universal result, not the finite q checks. value.rationale: The dyadic paperfolding word is a canonical automatic sequence, and scattered-subsequence universality and shortest-absent-word multiplicity are natural algorithmic and combinatorial invariants. A single local transfer mechanism yields exact exponential counts uniformly for an infinite, nontrivial 16-block class and all dyadic prefixes. This is finer than generic absent-subsequence algorithms or contiguous-factor complexity.
